rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An analogy about permanence helps only if the comparison case is known; the afterlife heavens and their endless duration are not known to most people, making the comparison uninformative.
rows.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : التشبيه إنما يحسن ويجوز إذا كان حال المشبه به معلوما مقررا

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Arab idiom uses the duration of heaven and earth, night and day, seas, or mountains to mean endless permanence, and the Qur'an addresses Arabs in their idiom.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في الجواب قالوا إن العرب يعبرون عن الدوام والأبد بقولهم

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: If the phrase bars punishment from continuing after the heavens end, it entails punishment's termination; if it does not, the idiom reply was unnecessary, so that reply fails either way.
rows.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : هل تسلمون أن قول القائل : خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse affirms that their punishment lasts whenever the heavens and earth last; denying that condition does not prove punishment ends, just as denying someone is human does not prove they are not an animal.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الجواب الحق عندي في هذا الباب شيء آخر ، وهو أن المعهود من الآية أنه متى كانت السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison still benefits readers by conveying an immense duration beyond the mind's grasp; whether that duration has an end is established by other proofs.
rows.anchor: قلنا بل فيه أعظم الفوائد وهو أنه يدل على نفاذ ذلك العذاب دهرا دهرا ، وزمانا لا يحيط العقل

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة وابن الأنباري والفراء
rows.claim: They treat the exception as a disclaimer God will never enact, like a speaker vowing to strike someone unless he sees otherwise while still intending to strike.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي ذكره ابن قتيبة وابن الأنباري والفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the disclaimer analogy: the verse states an exception for a period God willed, so the wording entails that this will occurred, unlike the merely hypothetical change of mind in the example.
rows.anchor: هذا ضعيف لأنه إذا قال : لأضربنك إلا أن أرى غير ذلك ، معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed reading takes illa as 'beyond': the phrase first names the longest span Arabs knew, then adds duration without end as an increase beyond it.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في الجواب أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposal excludes the time the damned stand for judgment, when they are not yet in Hell.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثالث : في الجواب وهو أن المراد من هذا الاستثناء زمان وقوفهم في الموقف

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says the exception may be their time in the grave or, alternatively, the duration of their worldly lives; afterward they enter Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الأصم المراد إلا ما شاء ربك وهو حال كونهم في القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal attaches the exception to their sighing and gasping: once they become motionless, that combined condition ceases even though they remain in Hell.
rows.anchor: الوجه الرابع : في الجواب قالوا : الاستثناء يرجع إلى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal says the damned may be moved out of the fire into extreme cold or other forms of torment, making the exception refer to their time outside the fire.
rows.anchor: الوجه الخامس : في الجواب أن يحمل هذا الاستثناء على أن أهل العذاب

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some scholars say the exception removes monotheist sinners from Hell's everlasting sentence: since unbelievers remain forever, those exempted from that rule are sinful Muslims; Razi calls this a strong argument.
rows.anchor: الوجه السادس : في الجواب قال قوم : هذا الاستثناء يفيد إخراج أهل التوحيد من النار

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An objection asks whether this reading works only after the other explanations fail and notes that an exception also appears for the blessed.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : فهذا الوجه إنما يتعين إذا فسدت سائر الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects reading illa as 'beyond' because it departs from the apparent sense of the exception.
rows.anchor: أما حمل كلمة ( إلا ) على سوى فهو عدول عن الظاهر

words: خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects exclusions for worldly life, the grave, or judgment: the exception concerns everlasting residence in Hell, which cannot exist before entry into Hell.
rows.anchor: عن الخلود في النار ، ومن المعلوم أن الخلود في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects attaching the exception to sighing and gasping as another departure from the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: فهذا أيضا ترك للظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects transfer to extreme cold as the exception: authentic reports say people move between fire and cold repeatedly each day, not only after the heavens' duration ends.
rows.anchor: والأخبار الصحيحة دلت على أن النقل من النار إلى الزمهرير وبالعكس يحصل في كل يوم مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community agrees that nobody enters Paradise and later leaves for Hell, so the exception for the blessed needs interpretation; no such consensus constrains the apparent reading for the damned.
rows.anchor: أجمعت الأمة على أنه يمتنع أن يقال : إن أحدا يدخل الجنة ثم يخرج منها إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the exception removes sinful believers from Hell, the verse's assertion that God does what He wills fittingly joins His display of power with mercy: no one has a claim over Him.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر هذا الاستثناء قال : { إن ربك فعال لما يريد } وهذا يحسن انطباقه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read saʿidū with ḍamma on the sīn; the other readers use fatḥa. The ḍamma reflects dropping the augment from asʿada; saʿida and asʿada have the same sense.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم { سعدوا } بضم السين والباقون بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ḍamma reading is possible by removing the added form from asʿada; saʿida is intransitive while asʿada is transitive, though both mean the same, as reflected in the name al-Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاز ضم السين لأنه على حذف الزيادة من أسعد ولأن سعد لا يتعدى وأسعد يتعدى وسعد وأسعد بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the blessed, Razi adds that some may be raised from Paradise to the Throne or to exalted stations known only to God.
rows.anchor: وههنا وجه آخر وهو أنه ربما اتفق لبعضهم أن يرفع من الجنة إلى العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root jadhdha means to cut, so God's gift described as ghayr majdhūdh is uncut or uninterrupted; compare the Garden's bounty as 'neither cut off nor withheld.'
rows.anchor: جذه يجذه جذا إذا قطعه وجذ الله دابرهم ، فقوله : { غير مجذوذ } أي غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the blessed are explicitly told that their gift is not cut off while the damned receive no such clarification, Razi infers that their exception means termination.
rows.anchor: فلما خص هذا الموضع بهذا البيان ولم يذكر ذلك في جانب الأشقياء دل ذلك على أن المراد من ذلك الاستثناء هو الانقطاع

none: The segment contains no commentary, only a slash.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the destruction of earlier peoples, Razi gives the absence of people who forbade corruption as its first cause.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما بين أن الأمم المتقدمين حل بهم عذاب الاستئصال بين أن السبب فيه أمران

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil is reported to say that lولا means 'why not' (هلا) everywhere in the Qur'an except in al-Saffat.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن الخليل أنه قال كل ما كان في القرآن من كلمة لولا فمعناه هلا إلا التي في الصافات

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshaf rejects that attribution, citing Qur'anic lولا clauses outside al-Saffat at 68:49, 48:25, and 17:74.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وما صحت هذه الرواية عنه بدليل قوله تعالى في غير الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ūlū baqiyya means people of virtue and goodness: the best of what a person gives is what he keeps back, hence the idiom for the best people and the proverb about hidden treasures and human remnants.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { أولوا بقية } فالمعنى أولو فضل وخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes baqiyya as baqwā, like taqiyya for taqwā: people who persist in guarding themselves from God's displeasure.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى كالتقية بمعنى التقوى أي فهلا كان منهم ذو بقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ūlū baqiyya on the pattern of laqiya, from a verb meaning to watch or await; it describes people watchful and fearful of God's vengeance.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { أولوا بقية } بوزن لقية من بقاه يبقيه إذا راقبه وانتظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception cannot be connected to the call for people of virtue to forbid corruption, which would absurdly exempt the few saved from that encouragement; it is disconnected: only a few of the saved forbade it.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { إلا قليلا } ولا يمكن جعله استثناء متصلا لأنه على هذا التقدير يكون ذلك ترغيبا

words: وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مَآ أُتْرِفُوا۟ فِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second cause of exterminating punishment was that wrongdoers followed what they luxuriated in, neglecting the central religious duty to command right and forbid wrong while pursuing desires, pleasures, and status.
rows.anchor: والسبب الثاني : لنزول عذاب الاستئصال قوله : { واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraf is luxury; a well-nourished child is called mutraf, and a mutraf is someone whom comfort and abundant living have made insolent.
rows.anchor: والترفه النعمة وصبي مترف إذا كان منعم البدن ، والمترف الذي أبطرته النعمة وسعة المعيشة

words: وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مَآ أُتْرِفُوا۟ فِيهِ
rows.speaker: أبو عمرو في رواية الجعفي
rows.claim: Abu Amr, in al-Jaʿfi's transmission, reads ittabaʿa; the sense is that the wrongdoers followed unlawful things in which they had been indulged.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية الجعفي { واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا } أي واتبعوا حراما أترفوا فيه

none: The segment quotes verses without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything is set to a precise measure that it neither exceeds nor falls short of, as also stated at 54:49 and 25:2.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى : { وكل شيء عنده بمقدار } فمعناه : بقدر واحد لا يجاوزه ولا ينقص عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes 'with Him' as God's knowledge: He knows each thing's quantity and quality in detail, so these known facts cannot change.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد من العندية العلم ومعناه : أنه تعالى يعلم كمية كل شيء وكيفيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes 'with Him' to mean that God's eternal will assigns each event a particular time and state.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد من العندية أنه تعالى خصص كل حادث بوقت معين وحالة معينة بمشيئته الأزلية

rows.speaker: حكماء الإسلام
rows.claim: The philosophers say God established universal principles with powers and properties, whose measured motions yield particular events and relations; Razi says human acts, states, and thoughts fall under the verse, refuting the Mu'tazilites.
rows.anchor: وعند حكماء الإسلام أنه تعالى وضع أشياء كلية وأودع فيها قوى وخواص ، وحركها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as God's knowledge of what is hidden from creation and what they witness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يريد علم ما غاب عن خلقه وما شهدوه

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says that on Ibn Abbas's explanation, ghayb is an absent or hidden thing and shahāda is a present or witnessed thing.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : فعلى هذا ( الغيب ) مصدر يريد به الغائب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported interpretation defines the hidden as what is known and the manifest as what exists.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الغائب هو المعلوم ، والشاهد هو الموجود

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation distinguishes what is beyond the senses from what is present to the senses.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : الغائب ما غاب عن الحس ، والشاهد ما حضر

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A third interpretation calls what creatures do not know hidden and what they know manifest.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : الغائب ما لا يعرفه الخلق ، والشاهد ما يعرفه الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi classifies known things as existent or nonexistent, each either necessarily so or possibly otherwise, and says God knows every category and its properties.
rows.anchor: ونقول : المعلومات قسمان : المعلومات والموجودات ، والمعدومات منها معدومات يمتنع وجودها

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: Imam al-Haramayn says God's known objects are infinite and each has infinitely many possible states; God knows in detail every possible location and quality of an indivisible atom.
rows.anchor: عن إمام الحرمين رحمهم الله تعالى أنه كان يقول لله تعالى معلومات لا نهاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot be 'great' in body, volume, or size; the word therefore denotes greatness in power and divine measures.
rows.anchor: وهو تعالى يمتنع أن يكون كبيرا بحسب الجثة والحجم والمقدار ، فوجب أن يكون كبيرا بحسب القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutaʿāl means God is exalted above anything impermissible, in His essence, attributes, and acts.
rows.anchor: ثم وصف تعالى نفسه بأنه المتعال وهو المتنزه عن كل ما لا يجوز عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's complete knowledge, power, and transcendence establish His ability to resurrect, give the signs disbelievers demand, and punish them; He delays these by will according to one group and by wisdom according to another.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية دالة على كونه تعالى موصوفا بالعلم الكامل والقدرة التامة ، ومنزها عن كل ما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the yāʾ in al-mutaʿālī in both connected and paused recitation; the other readers drop it in both for ease.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ( المتعالي ) بإثبات الياء في الوقف والوصل على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawaʾ may be a verbal noun, with an understood 'possessors of equality' as in the example 'Zayd and Amr are just'; or it may mean 'equal' without ellipsis.
rows.anchor: الأول : أن سواء مصدر والمعنى : ذو سواء كما تقول : عدل زيد وعمرو أي ذوا عدل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: If sawaʾ means mustawin, Sibawayh considers it awkward to begin a sentence with an indefinite active participle.
rows.anchor: إلا أن سيبويه يستقبح أن يقول مستو زيد وعمرو لأن أسماء الفاعلين إذا كانت نكرات لا يبدأ بها

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: A hypothetical respondent prefers the adjective analysis because it avoids supplying an omitted word, which is against the default.
rows.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : بل هذا الوجه أولى لأن حمل الكلام عليه يغني عن التزام الإضمار

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They gloss sarib as openly moving along one's path; the verse therefore covers a person hidden in darkness and one visible on the roads, both fully known to God.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : ظاهر بالنهار في سربه أي طريقه

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari illustrates saraba with camels going openly across the land wherever they wish.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري : تقول العرب سربت الإبل تسرب سربا ، أي مضت في الأرض ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether a person hides in darkness or appears on public roads, God's knowledge encompasses both.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الآية سواء كان الإنسان مستخفيا في الظلمات أو كان ظاهرا في الطرقات ، فعلم الله تعالى محيط بالكل

words: مَنْ أَسَرَّ الْقَوْلَ وَمَنْ جَهَرَ بِهِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse equally covers what hearts conceal and tongues disclose.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : سواء ما أضمرته القلوب وأظهرته الألسنة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse equally includes people who commit vile acts in the darkness of night and those who do so openly during the day.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : سواء من يقدم على القبائح في ظلمات الليالي ، ومن يأتي بها في النهار الظاهر

rows.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and Qutrub report the reverse: mukhafi means apparent, while sarib means concealed or hidden away.
rows.anchor: نقله الواحدي عن الأخفش وقطرب أنه قال : المستخفي الظاهر والسارب المتواري

rows.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
rows.claim: Their usage is supported by expressions in which khafiya or akhfā means 'made apparent' and ikhtafā means 'extracted'; a grave robber is called mukhtafi, while sarib can describe an animal hidden in its lair.
rows.anchor: ومنه يقال : خفيت الشيء وأخفيته أي أظهرته

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi judges the reversed definitions sound in Arabic, though Razi prefers the first reading because most exegetes adopt it and night suggests concealment while day suggests visibility.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : وهذا الوجه صحيح في اللغة ، إلا أن الاختيار هو الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter of Ibrahim has fifty-two verses and is Meccan; whether it is Meccan or Medinan rests on solitary reports and matters chiefly when legal material could involve abrogation.
rows.anchor: عليه السلام خمسون وآيتان مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif Lām Rā is the subject, kitāb its predicate, and anzalnāhu ilayka an adjective of that predicate; the phrase identifies a named surah as a book sent to the Prophet for a purpose.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { الر كتاب } معناه أن السورة المسماة بالر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لغرض كذا وكذا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that what is sent down cannot be eternal.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : النازل والمنزل لا يكون قديما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that the thing described as sent down is the Qur'an's letters, which are originated and whose originated status is undisputed.
rows.anchor: وجوابنا : أن الموصوف بالنازل والمنزل هو هذه الحروف وهي محدثة بلا نزاع

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites read the lām as purposive: God sent the book to guide people, which they take to show that divine acts and rulings are directed toward benefits.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : اللام في قوله : { لتخرج الناس } لام الغرض والحكمة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's school argues that acting for a further purpose would imply God cannot achieve it without an intermediary; since that is impossible, apparent wording that suggests causal purposes must be reinterpreted.
rows.anchor: أجاب أصحابنا عنه بأن من فعل فعلا لأجل شيء آخر فهذا إنما يفعله لو كان عاجزا عن تحصيل هذا المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr is likened to darkness because it is the farthest point of confusion about guidance; faith is light because it most fully clarifies the path.
rows.anchor: إنما شبه الكفر بالظلمات لأنه نهاية ما يتحير الرجل فيه عن طريق الهداية وشبه الإيمان بالنور

words: لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى النُّورِ
rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues that if God created unbelief in an unbeliever, it would make no sense for the Prophet to remove that person from it through the book.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : هذه الآية فيها دلالة على إبطال القول بالجبر

words: لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى النُّورِ
rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues that attributing guidance to the Messenger conflicts with God creating unbelief; an unbeliever could answer that if God creates future disbelief, the Messenger cannot remove it, and if not, no removal by him is needed.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أنه تعالى أضاف الإخراج من الظلمات إلى النور إلى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى النُّورِ
rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says the Prophet recites the book so people reason to God's knowledge, power, and wisdom, recognize the Qur'an's miraculous character and his truthfulness, then accept its laws; this requires acts they perform by choice.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما يخرجهم من الكفر بالكتاب بأن يتلوه عليهم ليتدبروه
